## Arthritis

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Arthritis, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
arthritis_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Health_Arthritis_LGA.csv",
                                   variable = "arthritis") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(arthritis != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
arthritis_lga <- arthritis_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(arthritis = dplyr::case_when(
    arthritis == "Has arthritis" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = arthritis,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Arthritis, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
arthritis_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Health_Arthritis_AgeSex.csv",
                                         variable = "arthritis") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(arthritis != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
arthritis_agesex <- arthritis_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(arthritis = dplyr::case_when(
    arthritis == "Has arthritis" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = arthritis,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 6.9% (n = 791) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have arthritis. This was lower than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (8.0%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have arthritis ranged from 134 (Yarra Ranges LGA) to 7 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have arthritis and the number expected if the rate was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Whittlesea and Yarra Ranges LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have arthritis ranged from 8.9% (Banyule LGA) to 2.4% (Manningham LGA).

- The percentage of people living in the NEPHU catchment who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have arthritis increased with increasing age for both males and females. However, the number of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have arthritis was highest for people aged 50-59 or 60-69 years.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

- Has the person been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Arthritis
  - Asthma
  - Cancer (including remission)
  - Dementia (including Alzheimer's)
  - Diabetes (including gestational diabetes)
  - Heart disease (including heart attack or angina)
  - Kidney disease
  - Lung condition (including COPD or emphysema)
  - Mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
  - Stroke
  - Any other long-term health condition(s)
  - No long-term health condition

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Back Problems

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Back problems
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
back_problems <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Chronic_Conditions.csv")

# Data wrangling
back_problems <- back_problems %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(noback_n = total_n - back_problems_dorsopathies_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::rename(yesback_n  = back_problems_dorsopathies_n,
                answered_n = total_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(yesback_prop  = yesback_n / answered_n * 100,
                noback_prop   = noback_n / answered_n * 100,
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yesback"),
                starts_with("noback"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yesback"  = "Yes",
                                              "noback"   = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 21% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were living with a back problem (dorsopathy). This equates to approximately 8,100 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely to be living with back problems than females (23% vs. 18%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Do you have any of the following conditions that have lasted, or are expected to last, for six months or longer? (Select all that apply)
  - Hay fever
  - Sinusitis or sinus allergy
  - Food allergy
  - Drug allergy
  - Anaemia
  - Bronchitis
  - Endometriosis
  - Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
  - Fluid problems, fluid retention, or oedema (excluding those due to a heart or circulatory condition)
  - Hernias
  - Kidney stones
  - Migraine
  - Psoriasis
  - Stomach ulcers or other gastrointestinal ulcers
  - Thyroid trouble or goitre
  - Slipped disc or other disc problems
  - Back pain or other back problems
  - None of the above
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, were you told that you have this condition by a doctor or nurse?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes (for slipped disc or other disc problems or back pain or other back problems), what is the main cause of your back pain or back problem?
  - Free text response

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Osteoporosis

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Osteoporosis
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
osteo <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Chronic_Conditions.csv",
                            iare_level = "Victoria")

# Data wrangling
osteo <- osteo %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(noosteo_n = total_n - osteoporosis_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::rename(yesosteo_n = osteoporosis_n,
                answered_n = total_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(yesosteo_prop = yesosteo_n / answered_n * 100,
                noosteo_prop  = noosteo_n / answered_n * 100,
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yesosteo"),
                starts_with("noosteo"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yesosteo" = "Yes",
                                              "noosteo"  = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 1.4% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Victoria reported that they were living with osteoporosis. This equates to approximately 1,100 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to be living with osteoporosis than males (2.3% vs. 0.5%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

  - Rheumatism

  - Rheumatoid arthritis
  - Other arthritis
  - Osteoporosis
  - Osteopenia
  - None of the above
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Do you currently have any of these conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Gout
  - Rheumatism
  - Osteoarthritis
  - Rheumatoid arthritis
  - Other arthritis
  - Osteoporosis
  - Osteopenia
  - None of the above
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Were you told by a doctor or nurse that you have any of these conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Osteoarthritis
  - Rheumatoid arthritis
  - Other arthritis
  - Osteoporosis

## Musculoskeletal Conditions

### Hospital Admissions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - musculoskeletal conditions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_musculo <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                               column_select = "admissions_for_musculoskeletal_system_and_connective_tissue_diseases_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_musculo <- hospital_musculo %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 2,064 hospital admissions for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 221 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 40 (Whitehorse IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 1,743 per 100,000 population (Craigieburn/Sunbury IARE) to 921 per 100,000 population (Knox IARE).

- 5 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases above the average rate for all Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Craigieburn/Sunbury, Whitehorse, Melbourne/Port Phillip, Yarra Ranges, and Maroondah IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - M00-M25: Arthropathies
  - M30-M36: Systemic connective tissue disorders
  - M40-M54: Dorsopathies
  - M60-M79: Soft tissue disorders
  - M80-M94: Osteopathies and chondropathies
  - M95-M99: Other disorders of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Emergency Presentations

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Emergency presentations - musculoskeletal conditions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
emergency_musculo <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "ED_total",
                                                column_select = "emergency_department_presentations_total_presentations_for_diseases_of_the_musculoskeletal_system_and_connective_tissue_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
emergency_musculo <- emergency_musculo %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- Between 01 July 2019 and 30 June 2020 there were 605 emergency department presentations for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of emergency department presentations for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 80 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 7 (Whitehorse IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of emergency department presentations for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 2,307 per 100,000 population (Melbourne/Port Phillip IARE) to 1,079 per 100,000 population (Melbourne East IARE).

- 4 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised rate of emergency department presentations for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people above the average for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Melbourne/Port Phillip, Maroondah,  Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, and Melbourne North-East IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Emergency department presentations for musculoskeletal system and connective tissue diseases are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - M00-M25: Arthropathies
  - M30-M36: Systemic connective tissue disorders
  - M40-M54: Dorsopathies
  - M60-M79: Soft tissue disorders
  - M80-M94: Osteopathies and chondropathies
  - M95-M99: Other disorders of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
